rawReview.evidence: SRD 5.2.1 permits Dash to raise a Speed-30 creature’s turn budget to 60 feet, permits movement up to the available budget, and defines 5-foot reach and Opportunity Attacks on leaving reach. The local Skeleton and Wolf stat blocks are legal Medium participants. The 30–60-foot route, reach exclusions, and obstacle-free geometry are coherent; no applicable ASSUMPTIONS entry or unresolved Table Decision blocks execution.

policyReview.evidence: The public scenario uses only permitted canonical SRD identities, Skeleton and Wolf, with generic independently authored prose and no protected PHB+ identity, expression, mapping, or crosswalk.

scenarioQuality.evidence: The 30-to-60-foot Dash boundary, player-selected route, 50-foot objective, and remaining-movement projection are mechanically meaningful. The Skeleton seriously pursues reaching the blocking position, and the Wolf seriously pursues its authored later passage objective. Fixed canonical stat-block choices and delegated Dash/route choices fit the distribution preference; statBlocksOnly and geometryAssisted align with the configured purpose. The comparison covers all 19 admitted Scenario ids exactly once, retains meaningfullyDistinct, and supplies the required non-spatial dimension evidence and differentiators.

closestMatches.reason: It is the closest authored Wolf/Skeleton geometry scenario, but it exercises active pursuit, melee attacks, Opportunity Attacks, damage, and turn completion; this Candidate isolates Dash movement accounting before either creature enters reach.
It is a minimal two-stat-block open-space battle, but its purpose is full battle-path tracing with changing tactics and rolls rather than a single movement-only projection.
It also gives movement and route choice a future interception meaning, but it tests Disengage, Opportunity-Attack suppression, and post-movement target reprioritization, all excluded here.

materialDifferentiators: The Candidate isolates a Speed-30 Skeleton taking Dash, selecting a legal route longer than 30 feet and no longer than 60 feet, reaching a future blocking position, and retaining the resulting remaining-movement projection.

The Wolf is only a distant future-confrontation anchor; the tested sequence deliberately prevents reach entry and excludes attacks, target selection, Opportunity Attacks, interrupts, rolls, damage, and turn-completion behavior.

The Candidate removes objects, cover, elevation, difficult terrain, occupied-space traversal, Disengage, mounts, and other interaction mechanics, making movement-budget and route-legality accounting the exploratory purpose.
